title: Ethiopian Lamb Leg Roast
localName: የበግ እግር ሮስት — Ye-Beg Igr Rost
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Lamb Leg Roast — a whole lamb leg marinated overnight in berbere, kibbeh, garlic, and ginger, slow-roasted at low heat until perfectly tender, served whole at the celebration table. The Ethiopian Christmas showpiece.
longDesc: The whole lamb leg roast is the centrepiece of Ethiopian Christmas — the lamb slaughtered before dawn, marinated through the morning, roasted through the afternoon, and brought whole to the table at the Christmas feast. It is the most spectacular Ethiopian celebration dish.
steps: Pierce lamb leg deeply all over with a knife.
Mix marinade thoroughly. Rub into every crevice.
Bring to room temperature 2 hours before roasting.
Roast at 150°C for 90 minutes — low and slow.
Increase to 220°C for 20—25 minutes to caramelise the berbere crust.
chefTips: The overnight marinade is what distinguishes this from a quick roast.
30 minutes of resting is non-negotiable — do not carve early.
The berbere crust at high heat becomes magnificently caramelised.
cookingScience: See ETH044 for lamb roasting science.
sustainabilityTips: The lamb is raised specifically for the celebration — the most honoured form of Ethiopian hospitality.
culturalNote: The whole lamb leg at Ethiopian Christmas is the moment that the feast becomes real — the smell of the berbere crust caramelising in the final blast of heat is the smell of Genna itself. Every Ethiopian Orthodox Christian knows this moment.
